---
title: "MDEA–CO₂–H₂O: constant ion–water fit on Kuranov 1996"
subtitle: "All rows solve; the fitted endpoint misses the 10.9% total-pressure ARD rule"
---

## Result

The fitted reading-(A) model solves **82/82 Kuranov Table 2 rows** but has
**19.5432% average relative deviation (ARD)**, above the issue's required
10.9%. The 19 and 32 mass % halves give 16.5453% and 22.5410%, respectively.
The result is a failed calibration criterion with useful numerical evidence;
it is not a numerical non-result. Independent review and investigator
promotion for manuscript use remain open.

The fitted constant is $k_{\mathrm{MDEAH^+,water}}=-0.2297985443$, inside
[−0.3, +0.3]. Bicarbonate–water remains fixed at −0.0765. The smaller
column-normalized start-Jacobian singular value is 0.02194035, below the
issue's 0.1 rule, so only the MDEAH⁺–water coordinate was fitted.
The native log-pressure least-squares cost decreases from 10.75645410 to
2.75756683 in three iterations with no failed trials. This does not minimize
ARD directly or establish a unique parameter value.

| Model | Solved Kuranov rows | ARD / % | Solved Ermatchkov rows | Partial-pressure ARD / % |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Original Wangler temperature laws, reading (A) | 82/82 | 17.6485 | 101/101 | 47.6504 |
| Constant start | 82/82 | 32.5553 | 101/101 | 60.2291 |
| Constant fitted endpoint | 82/82 | 19.5432 | 101/101 | 62.4440 |

The fit improves its constant start but is worse than the original
temperature-law model on both pressure comparisons. Ermatchkov's 101 rows
were held out and are reported without a pass condition. Kamps 2001 and
Jakobsen 2005 MDEA remain unscored because their rows are not transcribed.

## Conditions and interpretation

Kuranov 1996 Table 2 supplies total bubble pressures at 313.11–413.16 K and
about 19/32 mass % MDEA, on a stoichiometric molality basis per kg water.
All four CO₂-free rows and the five rows above loading 1.2 are included.
The error metric is

$$\mathrm{ARD}=\frac{100}{N}\sum_i\left|1-\frac{p_{i,\mathrm{calc}}}{p_{i,\mathrm{exp}}}\right|.$$

For Kuranov $N=82$ and pressure is total pressure; for Ermatchkov $N=101$
and pressure is $y_{\mathrm{CO_2}}P$. The held-out set spans 313.15–393.15 K,
MDEA molalities 1.905–8.441 and partial pressures 0.12–69.3 kPa. The explicitly
requested 101-row comparison includes 13 rows above the issue's nominal
49 mass % limit (maximum 50.146%). Nitrogen in the experimental headspace is
not represented in this model's vapor; the full headspace is not reconstructed.

Decision D1 uses MDEAH⁺ with self-dispersion and the neutral temperature-dependent
diameter, through the Engine's charged-molecule ion declaration. Uyan 2015
p. 93/Eq. (10) and Wangler 2018 Eqs. (6)–(7) state the opposite convention.
The reproduction gate's 17.6485% ARD is numerical support for reading (A),
not evidence that the papers prescribe it. The high-CO₂ pressure shortfall in
the earlier source-line comparisons remains open; Wangler Table 10 and Fig. 14
are untested with this reading. Both ion–water temperature laws are replaced
by constants in the fit; other temperature laws and reaction constants stay fixed.

## Permittivity sensitivity and uncertainty

One evaluation at the fixed endpoint replaces the straight-line pure-MDEA
permittivity with Hsieh 2007 Eq. (3)/Table 3 (pp. 620–621):

$$\varepsilon=44.1399-0.046824(T/\mathrm K)-8.82158\times10^{-5}(T/\mathrm K)^2.$$

All 82 rows solve. Kuranov ARD changes from **19.54315195% to 19.50895456%**,
a decrease of **0.03419739 percentage points**, leaving the failed criterion
unchanged. Both functions extrapolate above 328.15 K; 61 Kuranov rows lie
above the measured 303.15–328.15 K range. This is a model sensitivity, not a
validation of permittivity extrapolation.

No confidence interval, propagated measurement uncertainty, parameter-uniqueness
claim, phase-stability certificate or process-use qualification is established.
Ermatchkov's source includes 33 rows below its stated calibration range and
18 whose reproducibility exceeds its reported pressure uncertainty. These
rows are retained rather than assigned new weights or excluded after scoring.

## Evidence and numerical verification

The [fit summary](results/refit-summary.json) owns optimizer output and metrics;
[fitted Kuranov rows](results/fitted-kuranov.csv),
[Ermatchkov gate](results/ermatchkov-gate.csv),
[start](results/ermatchkov-start.csv), [fit](results/ermatchkov-fitted.csv) and
[quadratic sensitivity](results/fitted-hsieh-quadratic-kuranov.csv) retain the
calculated and observed pressures, phase compositions and solve messages.
The figure reads those retained values and does not rerun the model.

[Numerical checks](results/numerical-checks.json) recompute all seven pressure
tables, including the gate and constant start. Phase normalization, charge,
loading and water/MDEA conservation errors are at most 6.67 × 10⁻¹⁶.
Replayed endpoint pressures agree with native fit predictions within
8.91 × 10⁻¹³ relative. These are numerical checks; the held-out comparison
is prediction at measured states, and no physical validation is claimed.

Calculations use merged Engine commit `8298c6029ebb8b467929badc4a223c580ec591ab`,
wheel SHA-256 `8897a0caab9f2508ed642f42c8b5226957fbe7035ed7bfdad71e4166798785b3`,
and MA57. See the [analysis README](README.md) for source locators, source-copy
verification, earlier diagnosis, exact reproduction commands and retained-code
responsibilities. Further modeling changes require a separate decision; this
study does not select a replacement formulation or parameter set.
